look_here_first: Check fully expanded middle leaves: deep lobes or dissections interrupt the leaf outline; opposite foliage and blue-violet rayless heads support Conoclinium. C. coelestinum has a simple toothed—not deeply cut—leaf outline.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Erect to spreading perennial, often arising from knotty crowns and capable of forming colonies.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite; blades ovate-deltate to ovate, roughly 1.5–4 cm, with margins distinctly lobed or dissected.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small discoid heads; florets lavender-blue to purple, without ray florets.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: About 3.5–5 mm in Flora of North America.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae about 1.8–2.5 mm with a bristly pappus.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: deeply lobed/dissected palmleaf-like leaves; lavender-blue fuzzy discoid heads; opposite leaves; perennial clumping/spreading habit; Joey's source under the familiar name Conoclinium greggii shows the low mounded/spreading landscape habit—use that habit with the deeply dissected leaves, not flower color alone.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's West Texas landscaping video labels this plant Conoclinium greggii; the project reconciles that familiar older name to accepted Conoclinium dissectum. The frame is most useful for mounded growth habit and whole-plant architecture.

key_traits.label: Reproductive confirmation
key_traits.text: FNA: corollas 2.5–3.5 mm; cypselae 1.8–2.5 mm hispidulous.

lookalikes.differences: Versus C. coelestinum: deeply dissected/lobed leaf vs intact toothed margin (PRIMARY); FNA fruit hispidulous 1.8–2.5 mm vs glabrous 1–1.5 mm (confirmation). Versus Chromolaena odorata: Conoclinium has shorter hemispheric involucres with 2–3 phyllary series, rather than cylindrical 8–10 mm and 4–6+ series.
